name: EuroSAT
description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images for land use and land cover classification.

creator.name: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
creator.affiliation: TU Kaiserslautern, Germany and German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI), Germany

citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2 [cs.CV] 1 Feb 2019
rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were gathered from European cities distributed in over 34 countries. Images were downloaded from Sentinel-2A satellite via Amazon S3. Satellite images associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas were selected. Images with low cloud level were prioritized. Images were recorded all over the year to capture high variance in land use and land cover classes.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentinel-2A satellite images provided in the Earth observation program Copernicus. Images were downloaded via Amazon S3. The satellite images are multi-spectral covering 13 spectral bands with spatial resolution of up to 10 meters per pixel.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Bands with lower spatial resolution (20m and 60m per pixel) were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation. RGB images were computed by combining the red (B04), green (B03) and blue (B02) bands.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Image patches measuring 64x64 pixels were extracted from satellite images. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times. Mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice were sorted out and corrected. Images with extreme color cast due to atmospheric effects were retained in the dataset. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset consists of 10 different land use and land cover classes based on the principle that they are visible at 10 meters per pixel resolution and are frequently covered by the European Urban Atlas. Classes include: annual crop, permanent crop, pastures, highway, residential buildings, industrial buildings, river, sea & lake, forest, and herbaceous vegetation. All images were manually labeled and geo-referenced.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables applications in agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change monitoring, urban development, and environmental monitoring. It can be used for land use and land cover change detection, deforestation monitoring (relevant for climate change), and assisting in keeping geographical maps up-to-date (e.g., OpenStreetMap).
rai:dataBiases: Within one class, different land types are represented (e.g., different types of forests in the forest class or different types of industrial buildings in the industrial building class). Between classes, there is low positive correlation. The classes most common to each other are the two agricultural classes and the two classes representing residential and industrial buildings. The dataset distribution is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataLimitations: The classification system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with color cast. The classifier sometimes confuses agricultural land classes as well as the classes highway and river.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset can be used for land use and land cover classification, change detection applications, monitoring land surfaces, detecting deforestation, urban area development monitoring, and assisting in keeping geographical maps up-to-date.
